title: Executive Assistant to CEO — Reporting & Operations
description:
# Executive Assistant to CEO — Reporting & Operations



**Location:** Remote, Philippines  

**Type:** Full-time  

**Schedule:** Must have meaningful overlap with US Eastern Time



I’m the CEO of multiple growing e-commerce businesses. I’m looking for an experienced executive assistant who can manage my day-to-day priorities and **own the process behind my CEO dashboard**.



A major part of this role is collecting weekly report card numbers from my direct reports, verifying that the numbers are accurate, and giving me a clear view of business performance. I want someone who has run an executive reporting process before and can bring ideas to make ours faster, more reliable, and more useful.



This is a hands-on role with a wide range of responsibilities. You may be building a dashboard, following up with a department leader, organizing a project, researching a decision, or turning a voice note into a plan with owners and deadlines.



## What you’ll own



### CEO dashboard and weekly report cards



- Run the full weekly CEO dashboard process, from requesting updates through delivering the finished report.

- Collect each direct report’s weekly numbers, progress updates, blockers, and commitments on time.

- Verify numbers against their source reports where possible, check calculations, and follow up on missing data or inconsistencies.

- Keep metric definitions and reporting periods consistent so results can be compared week to week.

- Highlight meaningful changes, missed targets, emerging issues, and decisions that need my attention.

- Improve the dashboard and reporting process as the businesses grow. I want you to suggest better metrics, workflows, and ways to reduce manual work.



### Executive support and follow-through



- Manage my calendar, meetings, reminders, priorities, and day-to-day tasks.

- Follow up with direct reports on answers, decisions, and deliverables without needing me to chase them.

- Turn meetings, messages, and voice notes into action items with clear owners and due dates.

- Track important projects through completion and give me concise updates on what is on track or delayed.

- Research tools, vendors, and business questions, then present the facts and your recommendation.

- Draft clear
s, messages, documents, and meeting agendas.

- Take ownership of the unexpected tasks that come up in a fast-moving business.



## What I’m looking for



- **Prior experience owning an executive dashboard, leadership scorecard, or weekly business reporting process.** Please be specific about what you managed yourself.

- Strong Google Sheets or Excel skills, including formulas, dashboards, data validation, and troubleshooting.

- Experience collecting data from multiple people or systems and checking it before presenting it to leadership.

- Confidence following up with senior team members respectfully and persistently.

- The ability to turn a large amount of information into a short, useful update with clear next steps.

- Strong process thinking. You should see what is inefficient or unclear and bring ideas to improve it.

- Excellent written and spoken English, organization, judgment, and discretion.

- Experience supporting a CEO, founder, or senior executive. E-commerce experience is strongly preferred.



I’m looking for someone who can take ownership of this function, not simply copy numbers into a spreadsheet. You should be comfortable questioning a number that looks wrong, finding its source, and making sure I can trust the dashboard.



## What success looks like



Every week, I receive an accurate CEO dashboard on time. Direct reports submit their report cards consistently. The numbers have been checked, the important changes are easy to see, and outstanding questions have been followed up on. Over time, the reporting process becomes more efficient because you actively improve it.



## To apply



Please send:



1. A short introduction and your experience supporting a CEO or senior leader.

2. A specific example of an executive dashboard or weekly scorecard process you **personally owned**. Explain who submitted the data, how you verified it, and how leadership used the report.

3. A sample dashboard or report you built, with confidential information removed.

4. An example of a reporting or operational process you improved.

5. The tools you use most confidently.

6. Your expected monthly compensation in USD and your availability in US Eastern Time.



Please start your application with **“CEO Dashboard”** so I know you read the full posting.

title: Vein & Vascular Procedure Insurance Authorization Specialist
description:
# Vein & Vascular Procedure Insurance Authorization Specialist



**Department:** Insurance Authorization / Patient Access  

**Position:** Insurance Authorization Specialist  

**Employment Type:** Full-Time  

**Work Location:** Remote / Work From Home



## About the Position



We are seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented, and proactive **Vein & Vascular Procedure Insurance Authorization Specialist** to manage insurance authorizations for vein and vascular procedures.



This position is responsible for the authorization process from the initial determination of whether authorization is required through final approval, denial, or other resolution.



The ideal candidate has experience working with insurance companies, understands medical procedure authorization requirements, is comfortable navigating payer portals and communicating with insurance representatives, and takes complete ownership of assigned cases.



**Submitting an authorization is only the beginning. The Authorization Specialist is responsible for following each case through final resolution and ensuring procedures are properly authorized before the scheduled date.**



## Key Responsibilities



### Insurance Authorization Management



- Determine whether prior authorization, precertification, notification, or other payer approval is required.

- Initiate authorization requests promptly after receiving the necessary clinical and scheduling information.

- Submit complete and accurate authorization requests through payer portals, phone, fax, or other approved methods.

- Verify all information before submission, including:

  - Patient demographics

  - Insurance plan

  - Rendering physician

  - Ordering/referring provider

  - Facility or site of service

  - CPT codes

  - Diagnosis codes

  - Number of treatments or units

  - Laterality when applicable

  - Requested procedure date or authorization period

- Submit required clinical documentation and supporting medical records.

- Maintain documentation or proof of submission when available.



### Vein & Vascular Procedure Authorizations



The specialist may be responsible for obtaining authorization for procedures and services such as:



- Venous ultrasound and diagnostic testing.

- Varicose vein procedures.

- Radiofrequency ablation.

- Endovenous laser treatment.

- Sclerotherapy.

- VenaSeal or other vein closure procedures.

- Peripheral vascular procedures.

- Arterial and venous diagnostic studies.

- Other vein and vascular procedures as assigned.



The specialist must understand that authorization requirements can vary by insurance plan, procedure, diagnosis, provider, facility, and site of service.



## Authorization Ownership



The Authorization Specialist is responsible for each assigned authorization from **initiation through final resolution**.



An authorization is not considered complete simply because it was submitted.



The specialist must continue follow-up until the case reaches an appropriate resolution, including:



- Approved

- Denied

- Partially approved

- Authorization not required

- Cancelled

- Withdrawn

- Redirected

- Other documented payer determination



Statements such as **"I submitted it," "insurance has not responded," or "it is still pending"** do not constitute completion of the assignment.



## Daily Authorization Follow-Up



The Authorization Specialist will:



- Review all pending authorizations daily.

- Monitor payer turnaround times.

- Follow up on delayed determinations.

- Respond promptly to requests for additional information.

- Document every significant follow-up attempt.

- Establish the next required action and follow-up date.

- Identify procedures that may be at risk because authorization is unresolved.

- Escalate issues before they cause preventable procedure delays or cancellations.



**No pending authorization should remain unattended without a documented reason and next action.**



## Authorization Approval Verification



Once an authorization is received, the specialist must verify the approval rather than assuming the procedure is authorized.



The specialist should confirm:



- Authorization number.

- Approved CPT code(s).

- Approved units or treatments.

- Effective date.

- Expiration date.

- Rendering physician.

- Approved facility/site of service.

- Any payer restrictions or conditions.



Approval documentation should be obtained and retained when available.



**Approval of one CPT code should never automatically be assumed to authorize another CPT code.**



## Pre-Procedure Authorization Review



Before a scheduled procedure, the Authorization Specialist is responsible for confirming that the authorization remains valid.



Verify:



- The authorization has been approved.

- The procedure date falls within the approved date range.

- The correct CPT code(s) are authorized.

- The required number of units or treatments remain available.

- The correct physician is authorized.

- The correct facility or site of service is authorized.

- The authorization has not expired, been withdrawn, or otherwise changed.



Any discrepancy must be addressed immediately.



## Additional Information Requests



When an insurance company requests additional documentation, the specialist will:



- Identify exactly what information is being requested.

- Obtain the required records from the appropriate staff or provider.

- Submit requested documentation before the payer deadline.

- Confirm receipt when appropriate.

- Continue tracking the authorization after the information is submitted.



The specialist remains responsible for coordinating the request even when another employee or provider must supply the clinical information.



## Peer-to-Peer Reviews



When a payer requires a peer-to-peer review, the specialist will:



- Immediately notify the appropriate provider.

- Obtain the peer-to-peer deadline.

- Obtain payer contact information.

- Obtain the case/reference number.

- Identify the relevant procedure/CPT code(s).

- Identify the reason for the peer-to-peer request.

- Coordinate scheduling when necessary.

- Track the case after the peer-to-peer.

- Document the final determination.



## Denial Management



Insurance denials must be reviewed promptly.



Responsibilities include:



- Identify the exact denial reason.

- Obtain the denial letter or written determination when available.

- Identify reconsideration, peer-to-peer, or appeal deadlines.

- Notify the appropriate provider or management.

- Coordinate corrective action.

- Submit additional or corrected information when directed.

- Track the case through final resolution.



A denied authorization should not simply be closed without appropriate review and follow-up.



## Documentation & eClinicalWorks



All material authorization activity must be documented accurately and timely in **eClinicalWorks (eCW)** and any other designated authorization tracking system.



Documentation may include:



- Date and time.

- Insurance company.

- Portal used.

- Insurance representative name.

- Telephone number.

- Call/reference number.

- Authorization/case number.

- CPT code(s).

- Diagnosis code(s).

- Authorization status.

- Approval dates.

- Approved units.

- Outstanding requirements.

- Denial or delay reason.

- Action taken.

- Next required action.

- Next follow-up date.



Authorization documentation must be clear enough that another authorized employee can review the record and immediately understand the current status.



## Upcoming Procedure Review



The specialist must routinely review upcoming procedures for unresolved authorization issues.



Priority should be given to:



1. Procedures scheduled in the immediate future.

2. Authorizations approaching expiration.

3. Peer-to-peer cases.

4. Cases with payer deadlines.

5. Cases requiring additional clinical documentation.

6. Denied or partially approved cases requiring action.



The goal is to identify authorization problems **before** they result in a procedure delay or cancellation.



## Qualifications



### Required



- Previous experience in medical insurance authorizations, prior authorizations, referrals, medical billing, patient access, or a related healthcare position.

- Knowledge of insurance authorization processes.

- Strong understanding of medical terminology and CPT/diagnosis coding.

- Strong attention to detail.

- Excellent organizational and time-management skills.

- Ability to manage multiple authorization cases simultaneously.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills.

- Ability to work independently in a remote environment.

- Ability to consistently follow up until resolution.



### Preferred



- Experience with **vein, vascular, cardiology, interventional radiology, or surgical procedures**.

- Experience with eClinicalWorks (eCW).

- Experience working with Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurance, and managed-care plans.

- Experience with payer portals.

- Experience handling peer-to-peer reviews and authorization denials.

- Bilingual English/Spanish skills are a plus.



## What We're Looking For



We are looking for someone who:



- Takes complete ownership of their work.

- Does not allow pending authorizations to fall through the cracks.

- Is comfortable making frequent calls to insurance companies.

- Can navigate multiple insurance portals.

- Follows up without needing constant supervision.

- Can identify potential problems before they affect a scheduled procedure.

- Is highly detail-oriented.

- Can work efficiently in a high-volume environment.

- Communicates professionally with insurance companies, providers, and staff.

- Understands that authorization accuracy directly affects patient access, scheduling, and reimbursement.



## Confidentiality & HIPAA



The Insurance Authorization Specialist must:



- Maintain patient confidentiality.

- Follow HIPAA requirements.

- Follow all privacy and information-security policies.

- Access patient information only as necessary to perform assigned duties.

- Maintain professional communication at all times.

- Immediately report suspected unauthorized access or disclosure.



## Additional Responsibilities



Healthcare operations require flexibility. Additional responsibilities may include:



- Assisting with insurance verification.

- Referral management.

- Scheduling support.

- Medical record collection.

- Denial follow-up.

- Insurance-related administrative projects.

- Supporting new payer workflows.

- Other authorization-related duties assigned by management.



## Join Our Team



If you are an experienced healthcare insurance authorization professional who is organized, persistent, detail-oriented, and takes pride in getting procedures properly authorized before the patient arrives, we would like to hear from you.

title: Construction Bookkeeper / Accountant, QuickBooks Online (Cleanup + Ongoing)
description:
SarokaFi is a US-based financial operations firm serving construction contractors and service businesses. We're an advisory firm that does bookkeeping. Our clients count on us for clean books, clear numbers, and real guidance, and we're growing our team.



We're looking for an experienced **Construction Bookkeeper / Accountant** to join us long-term. You'll start by cleaning up one client's books, bringing several years of backlogged financials up to date. After that the role becomes ongoing monthly bookkeeping, and you'll manage **1 to 10 client books**. You'll work alongside our US team and each client's account representative. This clients books are needing to be cleaned up within 3 weeks. 



What you'll do



Phase 1: Cleanup project

- Review prior years of books in QuickBooks Online and find errors, gaps, and misclassifications

- Reconcile bank, credit card, and loan accounts back to the correct opening balances

- Clean up AR, AP, undeposited funds, uncategorized items, and duplicate transactions

- Rebuild or correct job costing so each job shows accurate revenue and costs

- Document what you found and fixed, and list open questions for the client



Phase 2: Ongoing bookkeeping (1–10 clients)

- Monthly transaction coding, reconciliations, and month-end close in QuickBooks Online

- Manage close checklists, tasks, and client questions in Double (
)

- Job costing, progress billing, and retainage tracking

- Track AP and subcontractor bills, including W-9/1099 readiness

- Prepare accurate monthly financial statements for our account reps to review with clients

- Communicate clearly and on time with our team



Must-haves

- 3+ years of bookkeeping/accounting experience with **US clients

- **Strong QuickBooks Online skills.** Desktop-only experience is not enough.

- **Construction accounting experience**: job costing, progress billing (AIA G702/G703), retainage, WIP schedules, subcontractors

- **Proven catch-up/cleanup experience**: you've taken messy books from years behind to current

- Solid understanding of accrual vs. cash, the balance sheet, and reconciliations

- Good written English and the habit of asking questions instead of guessing

- Reliable internet, a backup power plan, and a quiet workspace



**Nice-to-haves**

- Experience with Double (
) or another close/workflow platform (Karbon, Financial Cents, etc.)

- QuickBooks Online ProAdvisor certification

- Familiarity with construction software (JobTread, Buildertrend, Procore, etc.)

- Knowledge of Profit First, US payroll, or certified payroll

- Accounting degree or CPA-track coursework



**What we offer**

- Long-term, stable work with a growing US firm

- Room to grow as we add clients: more hours, more responsibility, and higher pay

- Training on our systems, SOPs, and Profit First

- A respectful, organized team that answers your questions



---



## How to apply



We read every application. To show us you read the whole posting:



1. Start your application with the subject line: **"Construction Cleanup — [Your Name]"**

2. Answer these three questions briefly (3–5 sentences each):

   - **Tell us about a cleanup project you completed.** How many years behind were the books, what was wrong, and how did you bring them current?

   - **A contractor bills 50% of a $100,000 job with 10% retainage.** How would you record that invoice in QuickBooks Online, and where does the retainage show on the balance sheet?

   - **Which construction clients have you worked with** (trade, approximate revenue, number of jobs), and how did you track job costing for them?

3. Include your resume and your expected hourly rate.

4. Note your available hours and time zone overlap.



Applications that skip the questions won't be reviewed.



Shortlisted candidates will complete a short paid-or-unpaid [TBD] QuickBooks Online skills test and a video interview.

title: Social Media Video Editor & Content Manager | YouTube, Instagram & Facebook
description:
Part Time | Remote | $6 USD per Hour | 12 Hours per Week



Do you enjoy spotting what’s working on social media, turning footage into engaging videos, and getting content published consistently?



Years Younger is looking for a creative, organized social media video editor who understands YouTube, Instagram, and
 and can help us build a stronger, more active presence across all three.



Over the next 120 days, we’re focused on consistent publishing, better content, and reaching more of the right viewers. We’re looking for someone interested in growing with us beyond that initial period.



ABOUT YEARS YOUNGER



I’m Kerri, the founder and teacher behind Years Younger.



We help active adults, primarily in their 40s, 50s, and early 60s, feel stronger, more mobile, confident, and adventurous through intelligent movement.



Our content covers mobility, strength, posture, breathwork, recovery, and helping the body keep up with an active life.



We want our social presence to feel modern, energetic, polished, and human.



THE ROLE



You’ll help take content from footage to finished, published posts.



You should be comfortable identifying strong moments in a video, editing them into compelling content, preparing the supporting copy, and uploading or scheduling the finished work.



Hands-on experience with YouTube, Instagram, and
 is required.



WHAT YOU’LL DO



Video Editing and Repurposing



• Edit engaging YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, and
 Reels.

• Find compelling clips within longer videos and movement demonstrations.

• Create strong openings, clear on-screen text, accurate captions, and purposeful pacing.

• Use music, B roll, graphics, and transitions that support the content.

• Adapt framing, text placement, and presentation for each platform.

• Edit long form YouTube content as assigned within the agreed weekly workload.

• Review your work for spelling, audio, cropping, cuts, and export quality before submission.



Uploading and Publishing



• Upload and schedule approved content through YouTube Studio and Meta Business Suite.

• Prepare platform-appropriate titles, descriptions, captions, and relevant hashtags.

• Check covers, thumbnails, links, publishing settings, and scheduled dates.

• Maintain a simple content calendar so we know what’s ready, scheduled, published, or missing.

• Track previously published material to avoid a
 duplicate posts.

• Flag content gaps early and help keep a steady publishing rhythm.



Social Media Awareness



• Stay actively interested in what’s working on YouTube, Instagram, and
.

• Notice emerging formats, hooks, editing approaches, and audience conversations.

• Suggest relevant ideas we can adapt to our brand and audience.

• Understand when a trend fits and when it would distract from the message.

• Bring ideas proactively rather than waiting for instructions for every post.



Performance Review



• Review available platform analytics, including views, watch time, retention, shares, and subscriber or follower growth.

• Identify useful patterns in stronger and weaker posts.

• Share a brief weekly update with what was published, what performed well, and what you recommend trying next.



WHO YOU ARE



• You have a strong video editing portfolio and practical social publishing experience.

• You understand the difference between a polished video and content that earns attention and holds it.

• You can write clear, natural English captions and supporting copy.

• You have good visual judgment and know how to keep an edit engaging without making it busy.

• You’re organized, proactive, and comfortable following a content calendar.

• You communicate reliably and apply feedback accurately.

• You can work independently within clear brand guidelines and agreed priorities.



Experience with movement, fitness, wellness, education, or a personal brand is helpful, but strong relevant work matters most.



TOOLS



You should be comfortable with:



• A video editing platform such as CapCut, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or Final Cut Pro.

• YouTube Studio.

• Meta Business Suite for
 and Instagram.

• Canva for simple covers and supporting graphics.

• Google Drive and Google Sheets for files and content tracking.



Descript and Dropbox experience are helpful. We can teach you the parts of our specific workflow you haven’t used before.



You don’t need to know every editing program. You do need to demonstrate strong editing and reliable publishing skills.



HOURS AND PAY



• Starting pay: $6 USD per hour.

• Expected workload: 12 hours per week.

• Remote, ongoing part time position.

• Weekly priorities and hours agreed in advance.

• Flexible editing hours with a regular communication window during my working day, 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM Pacific Time, Los Angeles.



Content may be scheduled to publish outside your working hours. You won’t need to be online every time a scheduled post goes live.



COMMUNICATION



During agreed working days, please acknowledge direct work messages within eight hours. A short acknowledgment is sufficient if you need more time to provide a full answer.



Please communicate file access problems, questions, or anything that could affect a deadline as soon as you discover it.



HOW TO APPLY



Apply through OnlineJobs.ph messages only. Please don’t
 the address associated with the account. Shortlisted applicants will receive instructions for the next step.



Use “Years Younger Social Editor” as your application subject line.



Please include:



1. Three video examples: two short form edits and one long form edit. Briefly explain what you personally handled for each. *Note: MAKE SURE THE LINKS WORK Before you copy paste.



2. Links to social accounts you’ve helped manage, where you have permission to share them. Tell us which platforms you worked on and whether you handled editing, captions, uploading, scheduling, or analytics. If the work is confidential, describe your responsibilities without sharing private information.



3. One recent content trend or format you think could work for Years Younger. Link to an example and explain how you’d adapt it for active adults in their 40s, 50s, and early 60s.



4. Your experience with your preferred editing software, YouTube Studio, Meta Business Suite, Canva, and Descript. Please be honest about what you know and what you’d need to learn.



5. Confirmation that $6 USD per hour and 12 per week work for you, your earliest start date, and your available communication hours in Pacific Time. Include any other work commitments that affect your availability.



Concise, specific answers are welcome. Please check that your portfolio links open.



Shortlisted candidates will be invited to complete a paid test with a clear scope, agreed payment, and deadline. The test will assess editing, judgment, content preparation, and communication.



I’m looking for someone who enjoys both the creative work and the organization that keeps good content moving consistently.



Thank you,

Kerri

Years Younger
